newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. speaker says candid talk needed with China.
newsitem.headline: U.S. speaker says candid talk needed with China.

text.p: U.S. Speaker of the House of Representatives Newt Gingrich on Friday met Chinese Vice Premier Zhu Rongji, telling Beijing's economic tsar that candid exchanges were needed to ensure friendly Sino-U.S. relations.
Gingrich, who arrived in China on Thursday with a bipartisan congressional delegation, was expected to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin later in the day.
"There is no greater impact on the future of the human race than the 'guanxi' (relations) between the American people and the Chinese people," Gingrich told Zhu.
"And it is very important that we talk candidly so that it can be 'youhao guanxi' (friendly relations), so that together we can create a better future for all people," he said.

Gingrich, who in the past has been fiercely critical of China's policies toward its island arch-rival Taiwan, arrived in Beijing hot on the heels of U.S. Vice President Al Gore, who travelled to Shanghai on Thursday.
Gore was due to leave China on Friday.
Gore's visit was seen as a vital step toward repairing Sino-U.S. ties that have long been battered by disputes over issues ranging from trade to human rights to Taiwan.

During the Hong Kong leg of Gingrich's 10-day Asian tour, the speaker warned that the U.S. Congress would be deeply concerned if China broke agreements on the British colony's future after it returns to Beijing rule on July 1.
China needed to understand that political freedom must accompany economic freedom, and America would not remain silent about the lack of basic freedoms in China, he said.
